claims.statement: EU Regulation 2024/573 requires operators of equipment subject to leak checks to establish and keep records for each piece of equipment.
Required record elements include gas quantities, additions and recovery, the identity and certificate details of service actors, and dates/results of checks and repairs.
The Commission describes qualified personnel, obligatory leak checks, and gas recovery/destruction among stakeholder obligations under the current F-gas regime.

contrary_evidence: The per-equipment record duty applies to equipment subject to leak checks, not every heat pump or refrigeration asset.
The regulation permits the Commission to determine record formats, which could force rework or favor official systems.
General field-service management products already provide asset QR codes, forms, and schedules.

economics.acquisition_route: Observe 20 real but authorized service workflows via local contractors, pilot with one 5-15 technician company, then sell through wholesalers and training partners
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated 5-8 year scenario: 150 contractor/operator accounts averaging 35,000 PLN annual revenue gives 5.25m PLN; at 32% EBITDA, 4x, and 75% ownership, equity value is about 5.04m PLN.
economics.founder_time: 15-22 hours per week, with scheduled field discovery and asynchronous product/support work
economics.gross_margin_basis: Mobile records, schedules, and exports are software; onboarding legacy assets and first-line field support are the largest variable costs
economics.payback: Customer payback hypothesis: saving 10-20 minutes of admin per technician job plus preventing missed checks can repay 120-250 PLN per technician monthly; measure during pilot
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: 1,500-6,000 PLN onboarding, 120-250 PLN per technician monthly, and portfolio pricing of 2-8 PLN per asset monthly
economics.retention_or_repeat: Records persist for each asset, checks recur, technicians change, and customers need history across the equipment lifecycle

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Longitudinal equipment/gas/repair histories and contractor performance data improve anomaly detection, renewal timing, and multi-contractor handovers
fingerprint.customer: Polish HVAC/R service companies with certified technicians and commercial operators of covered refrigeration, air-conditioning, and heat-pump equipment
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: HVAC wholesalers, certification/training bodies, industry associations, commercial property managers, and the family renewable installer network for workflow discovery
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Mobile capture, QR asset identity, certificate validation, gas ledger, signatures/photos, scheduling, customer handover, and export; hypothesis 120-250 PLN per technician monthly plus 2-8 PLN per managed asset
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Service-company owner pays per technician or completed asset record; larger operators pay per active equipment portfolio and contractor access
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Installation, scheduled leak check, gas addition/recovery, leak repair, technician handoff, customer audit, or authority request

founder_fit: Adjacent to the family renewable/installation business and local B2B operational automation
Data capture, scheduling, and anomaly detection fit the founder's technical skills
Can validate locally with bounded field observation rather than broad networking
Recurring asset records can become a scalable product rather than a manual service
risks: Technicians may resist extra mobile entry and continue using paper or existing field-service tools
Wrong threshold or certification logic could create compliance failures
Transition toward low-GWP or natural refrigerants may shrink parts of the recordkeeping market
Small contractors may be price sensitive and require high-touch support

structure.commercial_archetype: Two-sided field compliance record licensed to service contractors and commercial asset portfolios
structure.control_point: The complete per-equipment F-gas service, leak-check, repair, recovery, and certificate record retained by the responsible operator
structure.critical_dependency: Accurate on-site capture by certified people, correct determination of equipment subject to checks, and acceptance of digital records by customers and authorities

thesis: Planning-stage hypothesis: make a QR-linked service and refrigerant record for Polish HVAC/R contractors and commercial equipment operators. Technicians would capture equipment identity, gas type and quantity, certificate identity, leak-check results, repairs, recovery, and signed evidence at the job site; operators retain a shared audit record and automatic next-check schedule. The control point is the per-equipment record required for equipment subject to leak checks, not a generic field-service calendar. Starting through renewable/HVAC installer relationships could establish a local wedge, while normalized asset histories can later support warranty, gas inventory, and maintenance decisions.
title: F-Gas Certified Field-Service Record
uncertainties: Current Polish field workflow, incumbent software penetration, and record format expectations
Share of target equipment actually subject to leak checks under the current rules
Whether the buyer is the contractor, equipment operator, or property manager
Ability to verify certificates and share records across companies without an official API
